text_fidelity_a:
iHome iAVS16 Bedside Speaker with Alexa Built In, Bluetooth, and USB Charging, Now Supports Spotify by Voice This is a pretty mixed review of an interesting concept that is pretty good right now, but has the potential to be great in the near future. At the current price of about $150, this is ok+ based on the following criteria:

Sound Quality: 2.5-3 stars
For the size, it's ok
When reviewing for sound quality, I compare speakers (and headphones) to comparably sized items, based on speakers I currently or previously have owned. I take price range *somewhat* into account (I don't expect $15 headphones to sound like $500 ones), but for anything over $100, I use the full range from the cheapest stuff I have, to my favorite brand, Bose.
So with that in mind, I have a portable wireless Bose speaker that is smaller and acts as the "5" on the scale.
The sound on this can get loud enough to not distort and still fill a smallish room or normal bedroom fine. The treble and bass are ok, though the higher ranges are tinny and the bass lacks depth. Overall sound from high to low and throughout the mid range lack definition. It's good enough for very casual background listening and for podcasts.

Alexa Feature: 4 stars
I have an iPhone and think Alexa has quite a bit more understanding and skill than Siri. When asked questions, from simple stuff like "what's the weather" to more complicated stuff like "I'm hungry. What can I make in half an hour?", the answers and follow-up questions are highly intuitive and thorough. Does she get everything all the time? No. But she does a much better job than Siri.

User-Friendliness: 2.5 stars
I didn't like the process of figuring out how this works, particularly the part of pairing with more than one device and also Having to use an app to make most of it work. It was a clunky, irritating process that more or less stayed that way every time I wanted to use this thing, especially for listening to music. It should be able to just play from your iTunes through the iTunes app and bluetooth, and instead, I was only able to make it play iTunes though Their App, which sucks when it comes to my music. And that brings us to the App..

App: 2 stars
No. Just no. Bluetooth exists for a reason, and if a speaker has bluetooth, you should be able to just pair and play. I had to use the app to play from my iTunes, and because I have a very specific way of organizing things, I was incredibly annoyed that something didn't translate, and my music was disorganized and basically impossible to search for with this app. Instead of being able to play what I want from one of my playlist subfolders, it disregarded my way of organizing things, and I ended up giving up. If I can't listen to my stuff easily with this, then like 75% of the reason to use this disappears, leaving me with an expensive alarm clock with weather report, recipe ideas, and some cool internet stuff. That's cool, but it's quite incomplete for what I need, and what I suspect many people want.

tl;dr version: sound is mediocre but doable, app is bad, Alexa is super clever and smart, and the experience has a lot of frustrating aspects.
text_fidelity_b: iHome iAVS16 Bedside Speaker with Alexa Built In, Bluetooth, and USB Charging, Now Supports Spotify by Voice

text_fidelity_a:
Pentax K100D Super 6.1MP Digital SLR Camera Shake Reduction and 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 Lens First of all, I would like to start with highly recommending this camera to ANYONE who wants premium image quality with expandability, power and flexibility.

Pentax is one of the only companies out there that is driven entirely by photography and NOT by a marketing department that makes outrageous claims. To this end, even this, their lowest-end camera, is PACKED with premium features. Let's take a look at them:

1. Dust Reduction: Dust WILL get into your camera! This keeps it off of the sensor and increases the time inbetween cleanings.

2. Shake Reduction: It's good for a couple of stops of shooting leeway and you get it with every lens you use. Other companies build their systems into the lenses, meaning ONE lens can cost as much or more than the camera, itself! Lens-based anti-shake systems are more effective at long zoom than body-based systems, but unless you're rich, you won't be able to afford a suite of good lenses! With this camera, you can use ANY Pentax lens and get anti-shake.

3. AA batteries: Proprietary battery packs are NO GOOD. Hmmm, if you're on a shoot and your pack dies, you're not taking ANY photos unless you get a spare, right? With this camera, pick up some 2500mAh Ni-MH AA's and you can afford to get three sets. However, the power drain is so small, you might not need more than one set.

4. 6 MP sensor: Don't EVER get trapped in the megapixel hype. Megapixels mean nothing in the DSLR game, except for noise issues. Let me explain. The sensor sizes on almost all DSLRs (except for $5000 full-frame pro cameras) are APS-sized, meaning the sensor size on this camera and the Nikon D300 are very nearly the same dimensions. This means that photosensors on the chip have to be made smaller to get more pixels...meaning that the closer together/smaller sites are LESS light sensitive and they will also interfere with each other. 6 MP is a perfect sweet spot for noise and image sharpness. You get a base ISO of 200, meaning your camera is TWICE as sensitive to light as one with a base ISO of 100! This camera records color accurately and makes prints up to 8.5"x11" with no problem.

This camera has huge features and, even with the release of the K20D and K200D cameras, still maintains a good feature/image quality set with a proven CCD sensor and a suite of easy-to-learn features and settings. I LOVE this camera and even though I have a K200D for the weather sealing and larger burst capacity, the K100D super is the camera I ALWAYS take with me in trips. You're better off getting this camera plus a really nice lens and a 360FZ flash than a more expensive camera with a base kit lens and no external flash.

Believe me, this camera's quality will not fail to impress you and it will grow with you. It can use ANY lens its bigger brothers can and it uses them effortlessly.

A superb camera and one for the record books!
text_fidelity_b: Pentax K100D Super 6.1MP Digital SLR Camera Shake Reduction and 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 Lens

Amazon Basics 6 Outlet, Wall Mount Surge Protector, Power Strip, 2 USB ports 3.4A, 1080 Joules This AMAZONBASICS 6-OUTLET WALL MOUNT SURGE PROTECTOR (with 2 USB ports 3.4A, 1080 Joules) installs easily--all you need is a screwdriver (flat or Phillips). The surge protector is rated 1080 joules, which is much more protection than you get from most inexpensive surge protectors. This is plenty of protection for the power surges that happen when the power goes out and is restored suddenly.

Because my power company (PGE) delivers a LOT of unexpected power outages, I need surge protectors on all household outlets that service expensive-to-replace electronic equipment (e.g., microwave oven, coffeepot, TV, toaster).

This wall mount surge protector works well in my kitchen, where I have several small appliances that I like to leave plugged in. It also expands a standard 2-outlet wall outlet to 6 outlets. (This is okay, because I don’t plug kitchen appliances into all 6 outlets at once.) The surge protector has an orange light that tells you it is working. If the orange light goes out (for example, after a sudden power outage), then the surge protector needs to be replaced.

The two USB charging outlets are nice to have, but I don’t need them in my kitchen. If you don’t need these, you can buy a cheaper AmazonBasics model that is the same except that it omits the USB feature.

text_fidelity_a:
Creative Zen X-Fi 8 GB Video MP3 Player with Built-In Speaker (Black/Silver) Zen X-Fi 16GB review 2-28-09

Had the Zen X-Fi 16GB for two months of daily use now.

The device is well built and solid. It needs a silicon skin for protection, though. That is extra but highly recommended so your expensive player doesn't slip out of your pocket.

First, the buttons are too flat and are not illuminated. Sounds like a small thing, but flat black metal buttons against a black metal background in the car at night are very difficult to find and press. If the buttons were transparent and had the tiniest LED behind them, they would be a lot easier to manipulate accurately.

No Bluetooth--I'm getting very tired of wired connection to my car and headphones. LOSE THE WIRES, Creative! The earphones that come with the Zen are terrific. Really good quality. But the wires are tiresome.

Though I'd rather have Bluetooth, Zen is Wi-Fi capable. You can wirelessly hook to your computer's wireless router and play or copy files back and forth, but it's so frustrating to make it function it's virtually useless. USB cable is the way to connect.

As part of Wi-Fi, Creative does provide something called "Media Server" that you can access via your internet connection wireless router if you're in range and properly connected. After waiting a couple of minutes for the connection to be made, you can listen to propaganda from all kinds of politically correct content like NPR, the BBC, Australia's ABC and KCRW. Yes, master: I hear and obey. Mostly a waste as you can't really select content you want, only what they supply. Definitely politically correct. And boring.

It has a kind of chat texting capability but that's what phones are for these days and the Zen's dinky keyboard just doesn't cut it. The keyboard is laid out the way it is so it can emulate a phone keypad when you're in chat mode. Too frustrating to use. It's why QWERTY keyboards are on phones now.

Bookmarks. A few minutes after being shut off, the Zen forgets where you were when you shut down. If you fire it up an hour after shutdown or dock it to your computer to upload new content, it starts playing the last file you opened from the beginning. This is a bit frustrating when you're part way through a three hour podcast. So Creative allows you to set a Bookmark from within the file you are playing. It's quick and easy once you figure it out. I use it all the time now. This allows you to set a point in a podcast so you can return to it later. But while you can set the bookmark from within the file, you have to navigate to the Bookmarks screen to select the bookmark when playing back later. Not very intuitive. Took me two months to realize the usefulness of the feature. Why doesn't it simply remember where I stopped listening by itself? My DVR does. Just resume from where I left off. But no.

The lower left button is programmable. It's called My Shortcut. You pick from a list of available functions and set it. This allows you to go to a particular favorite screen or function once you decide what that is.

The Zen first and foremost is marketed as a video and MP3 player. What I wish it could do is have a "skip forward" ability (again, like my DVR does) that allows me to skip forward 30 seconds or a minute (or a user defined amount) so I can move forward in predictable amounts instead of holding the fast forward button down. If it's going to be called a "player" of any sort, it should have a variety of player controls. Skip forward/back should be available. Firmware upgrade wish, Creative.

Speaking of the fast forward button, the longer you hold it, the faster it goes. It starts by forwarding at a slow rate, then speeds up until you are jumping forward minutes at a time. This is good for zooming to a point quickly. But if you want to go forward, say, seven minutes, holding the FFwd button down too long will launch it into hyperdrive and you'll be at 10 minutes or more into the file, then have to rewind/search back. Somewhat of a pain. No. A real pain. Let me skip forward or back in 30 second increments.

A great feature is its built-in speaker. It sounds like my transistor radio from my childhood. This feature was the main reason I bought the Zen: you don't have to use earphones if you don't want to. It is a great and rare feature among MP3 players. A pocketable mini boombox.

Creative's Centrale "iTunes wannabe" software is dreadful. I tried it for awhile, then uninstalled it and now just drag files to the device.

Video screen quality is very good but 320x240 is still a bit small. Diagonally it's 2-1/2"; 2" wide x 1-5/8" high. It's also the old 4:3 aspect ratio, not the modern 16:9. If you're viewing a 16:9 video letterboxed, you are looking at one tiny video.

The video player (as opposed to the music player) is very weak. Windows Media Player 11 it ain't. Another key reason I bought the Zen is because it promised it could play a plethora of video formats. Wrong. I have dozens of wmv video files which exist in many sizes and bitrates from thumbnails to HD. Unfortunately, almost all of them need to be converted via Creative's stand-alone converter app or Centrale into squeezed-down bitrates and 320x240 size. This process is clumsy and slow.

If virtually every file needs to be converted in order to play, it's not really playing the advertised list of formats: it's playing the format Creative has selected and must be converted to. Often, even if I render out a wmv directly from my video editing software to Creative's parameters, it still won't play properly without conversion. Yet another marketing promise dashed to pieces.

The Zen allows me to delete files directly from the Zen if I want to (as opposed to needing to plug into iTunes to delete or add). This is good.

It has a built in mic and audio recording capability and you can program the "My Shortcut" button to start the recording process immediately so you don't have to navigate to the recorder's controls.

It has an FM radio that only works if the ear phones are plugged in because the wire becomes the antenna. What I'd really like is an AM radio, though, for news, talk radio, traffic and weather. Who needs FM? That's what your MP3's are for in the first place, right?

The unit has an SD card slot, but it's not well integrated. Content on the SD card does not appear in the normal file list. You must navigate to the card and browse it separately. Worse, when you do that, it comes back with "There are no playable files in this folder" even when I know I put mp3 files on the card that the player can play. You have to use the "Import" function to move files from the SD card to the player's memory in order to play them. Think of the SD card as an aux thumb drive, not as expanded memory, except it doesn't even work like that, actually. If you think you can buy the 16GB and "double" its memory capacity with a card, think again. It's more of a gimmick than a useful feature. More Creative fluff that is long on promise but short on delivery.

By the way, when you plug the Zen into your computer's USB cable the Zen does not mount as a drive (what Windows calls a "Local Disk.") It "docks" as a "Portable Media Player" according to Type in Windows Explorer. This means you can't play directly from the player. If you click on a file on the Zen from within Windows, it moves the file to a temp folder on your C: drive before playing. Not a big deal, but if you intend on connecting the Zen to a USB input on your car stereo or computer, I don't think your stereo will be able to see the Zen's contents. While the Zen is docked to the computer, all the play buttons are disabled and the display indicates "Docked" until you unplug the device. On the other hand, you don't have to unmount the device. Just pull from the USB and go.

Poor Creative. Always trying. Never quite getting there. Won't be long now and a phone will do it all. Look at Sony Erickson's W760, iPhone or Palm Pre.
text_fidelity_b: Creative Zen X-Fi 8 GB Video MP3 Player with Built-In Speaker (Black/Silver)

text_fidelity_a:
NETGEAR 8-Port Ultra60 PoE Multi-Gigabit Ethernet Plus Switch (MS108EUP) - Managed, with 4 x PoE++ and 4 x PoE+ @ 230W, Desktop or Wall Mount, and Limited Lifetime Protection I received this item through the Amazon Vine program, although the usual green writing may not be shown. The review is specifically for model: GS305EPP.

Port Binding: I noticed that the Netgear chart shows for the "plus" series of switches, that only models with 16 or more ports support port binding. However, through the web interface, I was able to do a single instance of port binding (it looks like it allows you to bind up to four ports, although I can't think of an instance where binding more than two ports on a five port switch would be worthwhile). I learned some quirks about port binding in the process, that using 802.3ad with multiple Linux servers doesn't allow for more than a Gb of data in any one direction anyway. BUT this switch does apparently support balance-rr, because I could get almost 2Gb/s over a 2Gb aggregate link. I think my hard drives in those machines were maxed out at that point. As I understand it, balance-rr has a high error rate because it uses striping and not all machines support it. But it was working quite nicely with my NAS units and this switch (I was expecting the 8 port switch, which would have made that setup more worthwhile because I could fatten the links on all three servers.

Although my current Netgear Pro AP does not have two ports for binding, I did have an AP before that supported it, in which case that feature on this switch may be an excellent option (particularly considering it is PoE). I haven't done the math for myself, but I think that port binding is almost a gimmick on APs because there is so much overhead on WiFi that even if your AP has a throughput in the multi-Gb range, enough of that is overhead created by the AP that you're not actually getting that much data from one computer to another.

Insight and Web Interface: The Insight App shows this switch (and my Netgear APs) as having "limited support" (just shows basic device info and a link to the device's webpage), so they're not really trying to get users of the "plus" line to subscribe to that in perpetuity.

And you don't need the app to use the switch. You don't even need the configuration page, really: I just plugged this into my old 24-port unmanaged Netgear workhose and it picked up an IP from the router and worked just like an unmanaged switch until I decided to give it a static IP and manage it.

I was really surprised how many features are packed into the management software, considering these are Netgear's lower line of managed devices. But most of the stuff you'll see on huge enterprise devices is here as well (well, it's been a while since I've been inside the big enterprise stuff, but all those goodies reach us as consumers before long).

The web interface is just like any other network device - you can reach it from any webpage and it is super GUI - probably just a little more than I really want it to be, but it is very intuitive and you can find everything with a few clicks. I say "super GUI" just because it looks fancier than I need it to. And one thing I find a little irritating is that when you expand one box, it collapses another, so you can't look at everything at once. This doesn't really matter, but I'm old school where I just want substance over style and even style that doesn't sacrifice substance still looks like they're trying too hard.

PoE: Clearly, on this 4+1 port switch, all four of your devices can use a full 30w each, so this is non-blocking in PoE+ as well as throughput. At time of writing, the 8 port with the same power budget was actually cheaper, so you might consider that, even if you can't use all the ports at full PoE.

What is great about this, is that besides just being able to add APs and IP cameras to your network (or even lighting, etc.), you can turn them on and off from the web interface. So I can keep my main AP on PoE (and therefore on my telecom closet's backup power supply), and then turn my detached garage's AP on and off from the web interface rather than having to go down to the basement and plug or unplug the PoE injector every time I want to use the garage AP (I just turn it on if I'm going to be working out there and might need to watch some "how-to" videos or control my audio system from the local LAN).

*Netgear, if you're listening, I would love to have a super lightweight (and free) app that works remotely (when not necessarily on LAN) to turn ports on and off for exactly this type of reason.*

Construction: Solid device, very dense and professional looking. Plenty of lights that tell you a lot from a glance. Power supply is external and about as big as the device itself. Would personally love a way to rack mount this AND the power supply (for maximum flexibility) in 1 RU, but of course I realize most people don't want to waste a whole rack unit on 5 ports. But for the space both pieces take up, it's about a mid size unit that could be mounted with "wings". It does have four-way keyhole mounts for wall-mounting.

Background: I have great experience with Netgear for my home (but way better than most homes') network. I'd definitely use all their devices were I doing work for small or medium sized businesses. I like them just a tad less when they start trying to sell you subscriptions (which is what I hate about Brocade and Cisco, along with all the proprietary garbage), but for the most part, Netgear is inexpensive and quite reliable. I've had a 24 port nonblocking unmanaged Gb switch running 24/7 in my dusty basement for over 15 years without a single fault AND they still sell that model. Their APs are the best I've had, and I don't think I've ever had a Netgear item break on me, period. I have had lots of other home/SMB stuff break or otherwise have strange issues, though.

That said, there's a lot of no-name PoE switches on the market right now. I don't need any of those handling my low voltage needs OR my data. And they won't beat this line on the price by too much anyway.

This is an excellent device which adds a lot of versatility to your network.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR 8-Port Ultra60 PoE Multi-Gigabit Ethernet Plus Switch (MS108EUP) - Managed, with 4 x PoE++ and 4 x PoE+ @ 230W, Desktop or Wall Mount, and Limited Lifetime Protection

I deducted a star for each major problem-no control over storage and what appears to be an unstable OS. I switched from another android tablet that was giving me problems. My brother has the largest Kindle Fire HD and it looked very nice. I paid extra to get rid of the ads because they were too obtrusive. One would pop in while I was doing something and shut down that app. I wanted a device for reading e-books and listening to audio books. I also wanted something that had external storage that I could manage. Wrong. The app saves to the external storage card but the downloaded content goes directly to the device storage which makes no sense. Why have an external storage option when none of the larger content files will save to it? The sound is more treble than bass, but it sounds good. My device is only 8 GB, so it max'ed out quickly when I downloaded content. I like the thin form factor. This cuts down the amount of weight in my bag. I got the magenta with a purple cover. Maybe it is because this is the first time I am using it, but the OS is very jumpy and the screen is not as responsive as I would like. I have to tap several times to open an app or play a song. Once I figured it out, downloading from my accounts was easy. Unfortunately when I tried to view my internal content, the device went into a loop, then restarted itself and that took a long time. If I ever am able to download to my SD card as the instructions say, then I will be happy to upgrade my review. In the meantime, I am disappointed that this is not able to do what I wanted.

text_fidelity_a:
PHILIPS 3 Ft. USB Type C Cable, USB-A to USB-C Red Durable Braided Fast Charging Cable, Compatible with iPad Pro, MacBook Pro, Samsung Galaxy S21/S10/S9/Plus, Google Pixel 5/C/3/2/XL, DLC5203RA/37 Thank you in advance to the Amazon VINE program for providing an item to review. A positive review was not required, nor was it requested, and all words are my own.

One thing I sadly use a lot of – phone/USB cables for charging and data transfer. These are almost as bad as the AUX cables for my car and iPod.

So, seeing this was a Philips one – I honestly thought I lucked out. I was going to give my old cable to my mom as hers was cracking near the "C" port. I figured I could use this one - she could have my old one.

It is a DURABLE cable and looked like it would go through quite a bit. The length is perfect for charging with an adapter connected to a power strip on the floor. And, it can also plug into the USB ports on a computer (or so equipped power strip).

So, why a one star rating?

This does not work. I tried with my phone and my mom’s phone. NADA. Nothing. I tried connecting it to the adapter – nothing. Tried using just the USB cable to a USB port on a power strip (which was on since it is powering my computer) – NOTHING.

So, I tried using a USB port on my computer. NOTHING. Tried with a “USB hub” connected to my computer. There was a slight problem. The “buttons” on the port light up when a port is turned on. Despite the port for this cord being on – the lights didn’t light up. Other items connected – my external mouse and a USB flash drive – they were turned off when this cord was connected.

Needless to say – this is BELOW one star. It doesn’t even work. But, I do have to rate it something.

I could’ve gotten a bad cable – after all, there is no damage to it or the packaging. But, it still doesn't work. But, I can’t return it since it was free.
text_fidelity_b: PHILIPS 3 Ft. USB Type C Cable, USB-A to USB-C Red Durable Braided Fast Charging Cable, Compatible with iPad Pro, MacBook Pro, Samsung Galaxy S21/S10/S9/Plus, Google Pixel 5/C/3/2/XL, DLC5203RA/37

text_fidelity_a:
TP-Link AC750 Wireless Wi-Fi Gigabit Router (Archer C2) I am not super "techie" like some of the other folks reviewing this router, just your average housewife who likes gadgets and tries not to drown in the constant wave of weekly tech improvements. As such, I wanted a new router to replace our two year old dual band Belkin with similar speed output, but only a single antenna. The Belkin had a number of dead spots despite using one of those extender things and I had had enough. Enter this TP-Link router.

I was wary of the installation after seeing some other reviews and the difficulties folks have been reporting. However, after reading the box and the instructions fully FIRST and then following the directions exactly, I had no problems. One thing I did notice immediately, is this router is meant to be used with a cable modem and that modem must be powered off before you connect it to this router. I used the website installation method and was up and going in a total of 20 minutes - that is from opening the box to having all our wireless stuff connected to the internet again. The website management page is very detailed and allows for a lot of customization of your network, honestly, more than I need or understand. But changing the router's password and setting our network name was simple and worked on the first try.

After three days of use I like it. The speed is decent and the dual antenna set up has improved the coverage problem we were having with the old Belkin router. I haven't experienced any slowdown or degradation of connectivity with multiple devices going at once thus far. A Fire Phone surfing the net, Fire tablet streaming music, laptop doing email, and a smart tv streaming video all at once in different rooms. So...a good router for every day family use in a pretty typical home.

*********** UPDATE FEBRUARY 2015 ***********
After 90 days this router is trouble free and really working like a champ. Our cable company upgraded our modem and increased our internet speeds recently, requiring a full shutdown and reconnect of my entire network. It was a snap and the router has had no problem with faster connection and the new modem. I relocated everything to the center of our house when everything was being swapped out and the router is now sending a five bar signal out to the back deck, which means I can sit out there with the dogs in nice weather to do email etc.

*****************UPDATE APRIL 2016 *************

I'm still using this router every single day for literally every single WiFi device in our house and it just does its job with zero drama every day. We now have two tablets, two smartphones, three DVR boxes on WiFi, two laptops, a printer, a Fire Stick for streaming movies, a smart tv connected the web now and then, and the Echo that's connected all the time. (yeah, I know...we watch a LOT of television in this house!)

Right this minute I am streaming music on the Echo, recording tv shows on two different DVR boxes, using my laptop to update this review, and uploading 42 photos from my phone to the cloud and pushing email to my tablet. Oh - and I am sitting outside on the patio enjoying the lovely spring day. This router is powerful and I have no dead spots inside or out in the backyard.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link AC750 Wireless Wi-Fi Gigabit Router (Archer C2)

However, when I tested them by tying them to weights and using them to lift, I found that they broke about 1/2 the time at 30 pounds, never quite reaching 40 pounds.

They are reliably good for 20 pounds without breaking, which is not too bad, really, for something so small. Webcam HD 1080p Web Camera, USB PC Computer Webcam with Microphone, Laptop Desktop Full HD Camera Video Webcam 110 Degree Widescreen, Pro Streaming Webcam for Recording, Calling, Conferencing, Gaming I've had this camera a few months. The install went pretty well. I had to reboot a few times to pick the camera up, but once it was recognized, that has worked well. The camera does not clamp securely onto my external monitor. I fixed that problem by getting a separate flexible arm that clamps onto my desk and holds the camara. I love the physical lens cover so I can easily control when the camera is capturing an image. The picture quality is great. I love having an external camera instead of relying on the one on my laptop so my laptop can stay connected to the docking station and I don't have to try to get it moved over to the center of my desk every time I have a videoconference. Unfortnately there there are two remaining problems that are making me now decide to look for another camera:

1. Echos: When using this camera, is it causes an echo on videoconferencing that others can hear. I cannot hear it. It is so annoying to others that immediately people start talking about it and asking if the call can be done using some other audio. It definitely happens on Microsoft Teams calls as others have said in the Questions section for this product on Amazon. I can't remember if it happened on Webex videocalls also. Others have said switching the audio source solves that problem.

2. Wide View: This may be standard on these cameras. I'll find out when I shop for a new one, but the view is much wider than my native laptop camera. I can't find any way on the camera to "crop" it so that it shows only the person during videoconference and not a lot of what is to the right and left of the person. I solved that problem by installing OBS Studio and the OBS virtual camera. OBS allows me to crop the picture and then uses that video as the "camera" in Microsoft Teams. That works very well to get a good cropped video, however, the image quality went way down and it freezes up sometimes, so it is not a great solution because I end up not having smooth starts to videoconferences with all the troubleshooting I have to do to get OBS, the webcam, and the conferecing software to all work together.

I hope I can find a camera that works seemlessly so that the now much more frequent videoconferences, thanks to the pandemic, will go more smoothly.
text_fidelity_b: Webcam HD 1080p Web Camera, USB PC Computer Webcam with Microphone, Laptop Desktop Full HD Camera Video Webcam 110 Degree Widescreen, Pro Streaming Webcam for Recording, Calling, Conferencing, Gaming

Victrola Retro Wood Bluetooth FM/AM Radio with Rotary Dial, Espresso I got the "acceptable" unit for total $17 (sorry), one foot pad is missing, I'll innovate. Firstly, I had wanted the chrome front but couldn't afford it and didn't want to wait a week; when I saw this used for the price I just pushed the button.

From the pictures you would think the front is all matte black, it is not. It's actually a very dark brown and the controls are a dark bronze, in shiny metal; closer to chrome aesthetic and looks far better with more tones than the photos would suggest. I'm actually happy I bought the darker color now seeing it. I tried to capture this on my pic, but it's too dark and still doesn't capture the wonderful appearance.

Plugging it in and turning it on was instantly satisfying, easy to use controls, no stiffness, good quality, lights work, radio is a deep amber or orange. Nice wood, looks and operates easily and great.

Tuning to a somewhat hard to get classical station locally was surprisingly easy and the signal came in loud and clear, unlike the other radios I've tried from Amazon. It felt like an old stereo where you didn't have to give it thought and was instinctive in the first 30 seconds without the difficulty and poor reception and static and crackling of tuning and volume controls or pops of turning it on nearly all cheap modern radios have now.

Bluetooth connected and performed seamlessly, perhaps a little softer than the radio but not horribly so. And the sound... On both radio and bluetooth the sound quality is superb; *just* enough bass without being muddy and the treble is good and clear. Bass in the voices and high pitches in the music, and very loud without screech or static at still low volume on the knob, with room-filling sound on FM and bluetooth.

This is the most pleasing product I've purchased from Amazon in a long time, especially in the radio category.

Update: After trying several others, I bought a second one! Like New $21. The only thing I notice is neither sits perfectly evenly, there's a slight wobble, even with all four feet pads. No biggie. Love the radio, excellent big sound, bass, but not muddy. Best radio on Amazon, and a true "table radio".

text_fidelity_a:
ACDelco 2-Hour Fast Battery Charger Includes AA Rechargeable Batteries and Car Adapter, 4 Count This charger works. It comes down to preference in style, and perhaps the going price at the time you are shopping around.

Upon arrival, I immediately unpacked this ACDelco battery charger. It comes with 4 AA batteries, and since I didn't see anything on the package about them being precharged, I went ahead and plugged them into my truck adapter. I was curious how well it would do in my truck (with the included car adapter) and since I knew I was running an errand that would take no more than two hours, I figured it was a good time to try it out.

I plugged them in at 2:10 pm, and saw that the batteries were charging as indicated by the red light. When I got back into my truck (I remembered to look!), the time was 3:05, and the battery indicator light was green, telling me that the batteries were fully charged. So this 55 minute charge time (likely less, since I wasn't in the truck whole time) tells me that it charged faster than anticipated, or the batteries had a little bit of charge on them to begin with, which is more apt the case--which is nice when they can be used right out of the package. Either way, it clearly charges and works fine.

(edit to add..) I see in the lower product description that the batteries come charged. Mine weren't fully charged, but I assume half charge (or more), and my charge time just topped them off. So to test this product further, I grabbed a set of drained rechargeable batteries from another brand that I hadn't gotten around to re-charging yet. I mean, I used them but drained them. I hadn't charged them again yet because I don't care for the charger it came with, so I just keep putting it off. I LIKE THIS CHARGING UNIT, and I will explain after details..

DETAILS!
--This charger charges AA and AAA batteries. It comes with 4 AA batteries and two styles of cords 110-volt wall adapter and 12-volt car adapter

-- The cord measurement for each is as follows:
74" wall charger cord
41" car adapter cord

--Charging Time Per Battery Capacity:
AA 1400mAh - 1800mAh: 1.5 - 2 hours
AA 1800mAh - 2300mAh: 2-2.5 hours
AAA 600mAh - 750mAh: 1.5 - 2 hours
AAA 750mAh - 1000mAh: 2-2.5 hours

--So, on the face of the charger on the left hand side, there are two indicator lights: one that glows red as the batteries charge, and one that glows green when charged and ready for use. Easy peasy.

--On the right hand side, there is a switch. It is to be set to either 2 batteries, or 4 batteries (+2, +4). Among the rebels among us, I have no idea what happens if we tried charging three batteries! :O

--Within the battery placement area, the slots are numbered. 1 through 4. I wish there were more clarification on this on the product page because I can no longer find the directions it came with. I am thinking that if just two batteries are being used, and they were placed in #1, #2 slots (or #3,#4) AND the indicator switched was in place for 2 batteries, does the charging juice primarily go to those spot (so as to keep with the quick charge ability)?. I think if just two batteries are being charged, then they go in the center, in the #1 and #2 spots-- so that's my plan going forward. I imagine this information is in the little pamphlet that came with the package. I'll be back if I find it and learn anything.

--The charging batteries at no point has gotten too warm my Energizer one gets pretty warm).

MY THOUGHTS:
--I LOVE that it has the TWO charging cords, with LONG cords. First, I like that it even has a cord, period. I have the Energiizer one that is just plugged into the wall. It seems like it would take up less space, but it doesn't. I find it harder to use as I need perfect clearance to plug that thing in. With this, I just need to find an outlet, then I can have it placed further away, making it easier to see and access. With the addition of the car charger, it just adds another option. Nice for camping (flashlights, radio, etc), or if you still use non cellphone cameras that eat batteries like crazy (this is what originally got me into rechargeable batteries almost 20 years ago, the digital cameras- ugh, I'm old). I sometimes bring a speaker with me for use with smartphone. It takes AA batteries. If I think to actually carry this unit around with me, I can charge my speaker batteries on the go if need be. But I think I will use this primarily in my home. I go through batteries with use of a couple of lighted mirrors. I have one that takes 4AAA and one that takes 4AA. The lights are bright, and I tend to go through batteries- so I make sure to have rechargeables on hand. As mentioned before, I like this unit because it is easier for me to find a place to put it to plug in AND have resting nearby. I had been in need of recharging a set of batteries and just hadn't gotten around to it because I don't care for the inconvenient (to me) charging unit of the other one. It works great, but I just found I prefer to have a cord. This has a cord.

PICTURES include another brand of (depleted) rechargeable AA battery (2000mah) with start time of being placed in charging unit. Product info says AA batteries between 1800mah and 2300mah will take 2-2.5 hours to charge. I put in the batteries at 11:42 am, and at 2:18 pm they were still charging. This would be just over 2.5 hours. I got up to take my dogs outside, and when I came back an hour later, the batteries were fully charged. So, I would plan on anywhere between 2.5-3.5 for a full charge on a depleted set of batteries (from another brand). Since I have yet to fully deplete the ACDelco batteries, I can't test those out until I do.

In summation.. I find nothing wrong with it, it works mostly intended.. If I figure anything else out as I continue to use these, I will be back to update.
text_fidelity_b: ACDelco 2-Hour Fast Battery Charger Includes AA Rechargeable Batteries and Car Adapter, 4 Count

It's 2022, I just bought a quality TV from a previously adored and promoted-by-me brand, and I'm super pissed. text_fidelity_a:
StarTech.com Dual Monitor USB 3.0 Laptop Docking Station with HDMI & DVI/VGA, 6x USB-A Hub, GbE, Audio, Universal Type-A Dock - Windows/macOS/ChromeOS (USB3SDOCKHD) I had high hopes for this docking station from StarTech but, thus far, I’ve been pretty disappointed.

Like many people I like the portability of working from a laptop but when I am at my workstation I want more screen space to work on - I thought this Docking Station would be a perfect solution. Well, in theory, it would.

Inside the box you’ll find the docking station, a 3.0 USB cable, a power adapter with snap on plugs to fit various world power sources, a DVI to VGA adapter, and a CD-ROM.

Unlike many docking stations or hubs this is not Plug and Play. I’m running the most updated Windows 10 64bit and the CD-ROM is completely useless. After inserting it in my computer I received a message reading that it was not compatible with my machine. No problem, I went to the manufacturer’s website, found the product, clicked on support, downloaded the zip file containing the setup and updated drivers for my OS and continued.

I went through the installation process and it appeared to install fine. After accepting the user agreement it checked my system for compatibility - finding no issues it continued and completed installation. I went to device manager and noticed an error in USB connected devices but figured with a restart it would correct.

I restarted but the error remains. Configuration Descriptor Request Failed - Windows has stopped device. I have uninstalled and reinstalled, searched help, used Windows Update to search for a better driver - so far nothing has worked.

In regards to functionality - the USB ports (two 3.0 and four 2.0) all function without issue and the Ethernet Port works great providing me over 200Mb/s. Due to not having the correct drivers I’ve been unable to test the multiple monitor capabilities.

I have contacted tech support and as of writing I have not heard back. If they are able to help me solve these issues I will update my review to reflect my further findings.

It appears this Docking Station is outdated being developed for older operating systems and while it may work for some users, others will find it needlessly difficult.

I would look at more recently manufactured docking stations that have been developed with the current operating systems - especially if you are using Windows 10.
text_fidelity_b: StarTech.com Dual Monitor USB 3.0 Laptop Docking Station with HDMI & DVI/VGA, 6x USB-A Hub, GbE, Audio, Universal Type-A Dock - Windows/macOS/ChromeOS (USB3SDOCKHD)

text_fidelity_a: Amazon Smart Plug, for home automation, Works with Alexa - A Certified for Humans Device We bought this plug when it was on a deal for $5. Glad we only paid that for it because the plug finally stopped reconnecting to the internet this week. Previously if the power failed it would reconnect on it's own. Occasionally it would just drop from the internet at random and then I could easily connect it. Most of the time, however, it would work great! We use it for a light since most of our house works on light switches that are not conveniently placed near the doors, so we trip around at night over stuff to get to the actual lights to turn them on without the smart plugs. Well after a storm and a power surge this past week, the plug in our bedroom showed as disconnected in the app. I have tried multiple times over multiple days to reconnect it. Once it gets to the internet connection part of the pairing "Provisioning Failure" pops up and it won't connect at all. I contacted Amazon via chat to fix the issue (after troubleshooting myself) and they only suggested resetting the plug (which I had already done) and restarting our entire home system and each Amazon Smart Device (which we did after the power surge due to other devices not working). After an hour and a half, they basically said well its out of warranty so you need to buy a new one. They did offer a discount but the discount was to be issued as a refund after purchase and the amount to be paid was significantly more then what I originally paid. We have 2 other smart plugs of a different brand that are as old as this plug that have had absolutely no issues to date and cost about $5 each when we purchased them as well. Not to mention the Amazon Smart Plug is bulky and takes up so much more space then the smaller round off-brand ones. Due to the fact that this plug didn't last a long time and the actual price is so high to begin with I would not recommend this plug. Spend the money on an off-brand!
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Smart Plug, for home automation, Works with Alexa - A Certified for Humans Device

1/2Mile Solar Driveway Alarm System-Up to 70FT Wide Sensor Range 3 Adjustable Sensitivities-Fully Weatherproof Outdoor Motion Sensor&Detector DIY Security Alert System I have been working out of detached workshop behind my house & set this in front of my house to capture the circular drive. It's not excessively far but it's out of range for a bluetooth device reach. It rings if anything goes through the circle (where the Camaro is) or down the drive past the house. I have tested it by walking at the very edge of the drive & it hasn't failed to alert. I may adjust the settings down before I move the receiver inside because it picks up a lot of cat activity. I didn't realize how many neighborhood cats stroll through my drive early in the morning.
I wanted to check this out before I committed to a mounting place so I set it under that oak tree. I thought it might be too shady to maintain the solar power requirements but it's been there a week with no issues. It's so discrete I'll probably just keep it on the rocks & move it closer to the tree. The mounting hardware is pretty nice, though, with a ball-jointed mount that sets up easy since it comes apart & has a lot of adjustment.
The receiver has three or 4 chimes & none of them are subtle. It also has another 30 or so songs. Some are holiday themed which could be fun if you were expecting guests for a party. It has some public domain tunes from the Baroque & Renaissance period as well as some contemporary tunes like "Music Box Dancer". I currently have it on what sounds like a mariachi band playing "March of the Toreadors" from Carmen which is kind of hilarious but I can't imagine what maniac would want to be alerted by that in their house ever. Most of the rest of the songs are like that.
text_fidelity_b: 1/2Mile Solar Driveway Alarm System-Up to 70FT Wide Sensor Range 3 Adjustable Sensitivities-Fully Weatherproof Outdoor Motion Sensor&Detector DIY Security Alert System

Sunhans Sh-2500 2500mw Wireless Signal Repeater 33dbm Wifi Signal Booster 2.5w Since there are detailed specs in the product description I will not repeat them here. Instead I'll use my personal experience with this kit to explain why I rated it five stars.

I used the review sample I received to extend the range of my ancient [[ASIN:B000BTL0OA Linksys WRT54GL Wireless-G Broadband Router]] (which is still working as well as when I purchased it ten years ago!) I removed one antenna from the Linksys, used a [[ASIN:B005IKGTXY Bluecell SMA female to TNC male Coaxial Adapter/Converter]] to adapt the included cable to the antenna connector, plugged it into the power supply and checked my home dead spot.

My dead spot is the master bedroom and my phone is always complaining about 'unstable WiFi connections' when I am in the room. I used an app called [[ASIN:B004EBZX6W Wi-Fi Analyzer]] to perform the before and after tests.

Before I installed this booster kit I was getting a strong reading of -45 dBm near the router and an absymal -80 dBm in the dead room. After installing this kit the signal boosted to -55 dBm in the bedroom, so this booster kit works as advertised.

It's practically worth its weight in gold if you do have dead areas in your WiFi coverage. Based on my experience and how easy and fast this is to install I rate this as a five star product.
text_fidelity_b: Sunhans Sh-2500 2500mw Wireless Signal Repeater 33dbm Wifi Signal Booster 2.5w

I've been using a much fancier (and more expensive) "computer stand" for a couple of years, but it finally bit the dust (the weld that holds the desktop onto the central support column failed). Of course I came to Amazon -- they have everything! -- and found a number of options. This looked like the best fit, so I ordered it.

I'm absolutely thrilled with it. Seriously, it's even better than I expected, even with my experience with Lifetime tables (which has been excellent). This little table is the PERFECT size for my laptop, a mug of coffee, and a couple of other items (reading glasses, etc.). It's lightweight enough that I can easily scoot it out of the way when I need to move around (get a coffee refill, etc.). My only quibble is that I wish it came in black, but that's absolutely NOT a deal breaker.

This feels far more stable than my old computer stand even when it was new, and it's not likely to have any similar problems. I love that I can adjust the height, too.

Overall, this is a solid 5-star item. Would happily purchase again if the need arises.

text_fidelity_a:
Jaybird X2 Sport Wireless Bluetooth Headphones - Midnight Black Finally seem to have found a pair of bluetooth headphones with acceptable connection performance. I was begining to think that it was too much to ask to be able to put my phone in my pocket and still be connected. Or to walk more than a few feet away from my phone and still stay connected. These ace those tests. Connectivity is not perfect but I am willing to accept that as it's bluetooth. I do get the occasional drop for no apparent reason but it is not often enough to be a huge negative.
They come packaged really nicely. So nicely you almost feel obligated to go slow and enjoy the experience.
You have to chose between the silicone or foam ear bud tips. The silicone feels softer and goes in and out easier. The foam will give you a more secure fit and sound isolation. I went with the foam and they do a fairly good job of keeping the outside world out. They are by no means 100 percent effective though.
I used the medium foam tips as well as the ear wings and find the comfort pretty good and the fit very secure. Wearing them for a couple hours was not an issue and I had no discomfort.
I cannot comment on their ability to transmit music as I use them for podcasts. Sound quality was fine for speech.
These have come down in price so much lately that I think they are a no brainer compared to the competition.
I dropped them a star due to the occasional random connection failure but overall I am very pleased with them.
text_fidelity_b: Jaybird X2 Sport Wireless Bluetooth Headphones - Midnight Black

The ERGO still worked but would occasionally get stuck when the support pegs would catch the pock and cause the ball to resist - not enough to really hurt anything but just enough to make digital drawing difficult and just enough to annoy me. This replacement ball has taken care of that for me and has proven to be a worthwhile expense for me.

The ERGO and the M570 have the same size ball, so this ball can be used in either (I was using the ball from my old M570 in the ERGO while I waited for this ball to arrive). Replacement is a 30-second procedure and requires no special tools, though a pencil does make getting the old ball out a lot easier.

There are two different finish types available, glossy and matte. I chose the glossy in red. Operation has been absolutely smooth with no resistance at all and no catches. I haven’t noticed any operational differences between it and the original gray ball that came in my ERGO. And, in my opinion, the dark red of this ball actually looks a little nicer than the original silver ball as well as the blue M570 ball.

This wasn’t an expensive replacement and so far it has worked out very well for me. It has restored operation of my trackball to what it was before I damaged the original ball, which is really all I needed. Based on my experience with it, this is an easy replacement ball to recommend if you need to replace the ball in either a Logitech M570 or an MX ERGO.

text_fidelity_a:
TV Antenna - 1byone Amplified 50 Mile HDTV Digital Antenna Powerful Amplifier Signal Booster for All TV 4K UHF VHF 1080P Local Channels with 20ft Coaxial Cable This is a review of the 50 mile OUS00-0562 model. To summarize: It works. But it's no better than my cheap [[ASIN:B000HKGK8Y RCA Indoor FM and HDTV Antenna]] antenna that I was trying to replace, yet costing several times more.

With my cheap RCA "rabbit ears" antenna I was getting 18 channels, being 8 miles away from the transmitter. According to my digital-to-analog converter most TV signals were in the range of 75% to 30%. I was looking for a better antenna to improve the signal quality, so when I saw that the OUS00-0562 model was on sale I bought it. I didn't believe the 50 mile claim of this antenna since most antennas with this claim are large, more expensive and rather directional. But I figured that even if it was half that it had to be better than my RCA one. Whatever this antenna was directional of not was not specified, I assumed that it was not.

The OUS00-0562 model comes with an antenna with a 20 foot non-removable cord. This was disappointing, but I should have realized this when looking at the product pictures. Having so much cable slack is a waste when it sits 3 feet from the TV. Before I installed the 1byone antenna I took note of signal strength of each channel of my RCA antenna. The OUS00-0562 package also comes with an amplifier, which I connected to my RCA antenna as a test - and was disappointed. Only 3 channels were 10% higher, and that was within margin of error. The OUS00-0562 disappointed me soon after, as there was no change in signal strength on any channel over the RCA antenna (except that it gave me two more channels at 40% signal).

The short version:

RCA "rabbit ears" - 18 channels, 75%-30% (+/- 5%)
RCA "rabbit ears" with 1byone amplifier - 18 channels, 70%-30% (+/- 5%)
1byone OUS00-0562 with 1byone amplifier - 20 channels, 70%-30% (+/- 5%)

I tried to reposition the OUS00-0562 antenna to see if there was a directional issue, if I was out of the "sweat spot." I did notice 5-10% dips here and there but no marked improvements. I didn't spend much time on this and since it wasn't shipped with a stand. You can buy one, but I didn't want to spend any more money on it since to me it was overpriced as is. I promptly returned it.

I will give this antenna one point though. It's better looking than the RCA antenna and it takes up less space. So if looks and space matter, it might be for you.
text_fidelity_b: TV Antenna - 1byone Amplified 50 Mile HDTV Digital Antenna Powerful Amplifier Signal Booster for All TV 4K UHF VHF 1080P Local Channels with 20ft Coaxial Cable

USB Multiple Plug Outlet, Unidapt Night Light Outlet with Surge Protector, 3 USB Charging Ports (1 Type C Port), 6 Wide Spaced AC Outlets, Wall Night Light, Fast Charge Multi Plug Extender, White After using surge protection for audio, video and computer equipment for more than 30 years I can definitely say not all of these products are created equally.

While surge protectors will often boast of great protection, more often than not they are more multi outlet plugs rather than actual protection.

I have thoroughly tested this surge protector and it has passed all of my testing. While only rated for 700 joules, this is typically adequate especially when your home has proper grounding. Often similar devices pass my tests initially yet fail after the 1 or 3 month mark - that has not been the case with this item.

The way this is designed allowed me to utilize this in my bathroom to have all of my toiletry accessories charging at once yet have everything compact and tucked away. It’s nice that this doubles as a nightlight that has adjustable levels of light and automatically turns on and off.

The only thing I wish was different was if on the sides the outlets were more widely spaced to allow for larger power blocks - with that being said having 6 outlets should allow most users to have more than enough.

The 3 USB ports are definitely a nice addition as this helps avoid having to use plugs for USB powered devices. There are 2 standard USB-A ports and 1 ultra fast USB-C port.

This is an outstanding surge protector and nightlight that has proven itself through extensive use and testing.

This is definitely a product I recommend.

text_fidelity_a:
Hercules Wireless Bluetooth Speaker (White/Green) I've been testing this speaker system with my 10" Samsung Galaxy Tab2 tablet which had no problems connecting to the speakers with and without the app from the Android store.

Appearance:
Their product description calls this 'fun, trendy and modern'. But to be honest this looks, to me, like an appliance that fell out of my grandmother's 1950's black, white and chrome art-deco kitchen. It's not unpleasant looking but I wouldn't call it modern. When I saw images of the system online I had hopes that the neon green ring around the face would light up. Sadly it doesn't. The handle is also fixed in place and doesn't retract or collapse into the body. It would have been a nice idea so you could stack or store this more easily.

Sound:
It doesn't sound bad. Especially for being just two 15 watt wide range speakers in a ported (holes to help the bass sound better) enclosure. The bass is a little flat and the high end sounds a little... hollow but it is a lot better than the speakers built into my tablet. I've tried a variety of music; jazz, pop, classical, rock, punk and everything sounded quite good. I found I had to use both the tablet's volume control as well as the speaker systems volume controls to get real volume out of the system. They operate independently of each other.

Drawbacks:
I don't normally comment on price with items received from the Vine program but at the time I'm writing this review Amazon is currently selling this item for over two hundred dollars. Maybe the Bluetooth equipment is expensive but to me that's a LOT for just two speakers in a box. I didn't pay that much for my four speaker bookshelf system or the subwoofer equipped speaker system connected to my desktop PC. Both of which have far superior sound quality.

The battery indicator light only seems to light up when the system is charging. I charged this a week ago and used it for several hours at a time but I have no idea how much charge is left in the battery.

The biggest problem I had with this speaker system was when doing anything other than playing music. I thought it would be fun to add big sound to the games I enjoy on my tablet but there's a distinct lag between doing anything and when the speaker plays the sound. I noticed it most of all in my favorite billiards simulator. You would strike a ball...and then hear it happen, even system sounds such as keyboard typing noises, a 'blip' when selecting things played a noticeable time after they happened.

The App:
I won't say much about the app here. It's completely unnecessary to operate this system with your Android device. It's just poor quality programming that appears to have been slapped together at the last minute. It also doesn't match the documentation and features such as Bass Boost which are in the instructions but don't exist in the app.

Speaking of the documentation. I opened the box and found a large booklet and for one, brief, moment I thought this item was fully documented in depth and detail... then I opened the instructions and found there's twelve pages of English instructions which are poorly written and lacking in detail. The rest of the book is comprised of numerous other languages each getting their own few pages. Ah well. Turn it on, turn it up. Enjoy the music.
text_fidelity_b: Hercules Wireless Bluetooth Speaker (White/Green)

text_fidelity_a: Seagate FreeAgent GoFlex Desk 1 TB USB 2.0 External Hard Drive STAC1000100 (Black) I'm one of the folks who had a hard drive crash without having backed up for several months.  That was all it took for me to realize the importance of backing up my hard drive regularly and not simply putting current files on a flash drive.  I'd been using a Western Digital drive for the past three or four years, then was told that hard drives have a limited life span.  That made sense, so I decided to replace the external drive which is used to backup my MacBook.  I almost purchased the Seagate FreeAgent GoFlex 500 GB USB 2.0 Ultra-Portable External Hard Drive STAA500100, then decided that I don't take the external drive with me and didn't need it to be portable.  Enter the Seagate FreeAgent GoFlex Desk 2 TB Desktop External Hard Drive STAC2000100, a shiny black drive that looks much sleeker and way more shiny than the dull Western Digital.  2 TB seemed like more than I need, but I went for it anyway.  Before the package arrived, I watched the videos available on the Seagate website, so I was prepared for this drive and felt comfortable using it as my new backup drive.  My only question was whether or not to format it for use with Mac and PC or just the Mac.  Decided on the Mac only and didn't install the other options onto my MacBook.  Since I use Time Machine, I immediately proceeded to backup the hard drive.  Not having purchased the optional Firewire, eSATA or USB 3.0, the transfer is not faster than on the other external drives I've used, but this one sure is quiet and it's much nicer to look at.  It also doesn't weigh as much as other desktop external drives.  Looks like the attractive Seagate sleek shape, just bigger.  There is no button to push, just plug in and connect, then go to Time Machine.  I cannot review the included Memeo backup because I've not installed it.  Can't imagine that it would be better than Time Machine.  This meets my needs and exceeds my expectations.  It also looks nicer when locked up in my fire retardant portable safe than any other drive.
text_fidelity_b: Seagate FreeAgent GoFlex Desk 1 TB USB 2.0 External Hard Drive STAC1000100 (Black)

Aibocn MFi Certified 30 Pin Sync and Charge Dock Cable (New Packaging × 2 Pack) This cable bears the MFi (Made for iPod/iPad/iPhone) logo on the packaging and looks nearly identical to the real thing. The only things different are there is no Apple logo on the cable and it does not carry the Apple price tag.

I tested it both as a charging cable and a synching cable with an iPad 2 and it performed flawlessly.

The thing that is the same is this is manufactured to Apple's specs and did earn the MFI certification. Why this is important to me is most third party manufacturers have dropped this legacy cable and are now licensing Apple's Lightning cable (if they are even MFi certified). Decent 30 pin cables are becoming scarce, and the ones from Apple are pricy. That leaves a lot of fly-by-night cables that have a high failure rate, and I am frankly tiring of replacing cables on a monthly basis (I had been purchasing them from a well known big box store as well as a nationwide electronics chain.) When I was offered this one as a review sample I could not resist.

I've been using this as my sole cable for over a week and am not disappointed. The construction is identical to Apple's, and the performance is too. If you are in the same quandary as I - experiencing high failure rates on 30 pin cables - check this one out.

Other pluses include an operational light that is easy to see but not distracting and a reasonably compact size. Operational speed has been more than acceptable on both USB 2.0 and 3.0 ports. The only notable negative is the case. It's plastic, as expected, but rather flimsy feeling. This is not a drive that will withstand any measure of being knocked around. An SSD drive would be a better choice if durability is the goal.

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech USB Headset Stereo H650e This is a decent, serviceable headset but rather expensive for the price. I have another Logitech headset for home use but this one was definitely better in quality.

Appearance: the plastic casing feels a little cheap, which raises questions about its durability. I once owned a Sharper Image headphone that had a similar feel, and it broke after a year or so.

Function: the headphone is lightweight and quite comfortable to wear, thanks to the padding on the top and the ear muffs. However, the muffs are thinner than I expected. For the price, I would have liked them to be thicker and offer better noise cancellation capabilities. The microphone, however, feels professional grade, being bendable and sensitive. In addition, the long cord is very work-friendly - it's thicker than conventional cords (preventing easy tangling) and long enough for me to reach over my desk without concern that it'll tug or pop out. Also convenient are the location of the controls for volume, phone and speaker - they're on a rectangular box located on the cord itself. Cool.

However, setting up the headphone took some work. With my other Logitech headphone, all I had to do was plug it into the USB drive, let the computer recognize the device, and off I went. Here, I had to be patient and follow the specific setting instructions for Windows 8. Listening to videos and audio files worked fine, but the microphone function didn't work when my phone rang and I tried ti answer using the mike. I pressed the button but nothing happened. As it turns out, the phone function appears to work only when you're hooked up to Linc, an application that nobody in my office uses. The instructions didn't make this clear.

The sound quality is decent for business purposes but for hi-fidelity sound, it's average. I had assumed it was a noise cancelling headphone because of the padding, but I was wrong - I had no trouble hearing some of my coworkers bickering a few feet away while I was listening to a webinar. I had to up the volume to block them out.

The headphones come with a smooth zippered vinyl pouch for storage or for traveling. This was a very nice touch.

Overall this is a decent enough headphone for work but I would have given it five stars had the price been lower.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech USB Headset Stereo H650e

text_fidelity_a:
PIONEER DV-610V-K MULTI REGION 1080p UPCONVERTING DVD PLAYER This is the most amazingly satisfying electronics product I have ever bought. The features are many and easy to learn. I especially enjoy some of the audio and video adjustment features:
Audio: DRC setting helps bring up quieter sounds while controlling loud peaks. Great for taming those annoying audio surges in 'background' music or battle scenes, etc. The Dialog feature lets you adjust the dialog perception so that you can hear the voices better over the background sounds in the soundtracks.
Video: You can adjust the Sharpness, Brightness, Contrast, Gamma, Hue, Chroma Level and BNR (block noise reduction). Each one has several levels to choose from and you get to sample it as it adjusts, so you can skip back and forth and compare the difference before you decide what to settle on.
The USB mode has great, easy to navigate menus. You can also record to your thumb drive from a CD that you are playing. There is a choice of different bit rates to do this and you can record individual tracks or all tracks. Very user-friendly menus for all these choices.
This unit has too many features to list, especially for someone like me, who is not quite fluent in tech terminology. Suffice it to say that it performs all the functions beautifully, the manual is very user-friendly and not only tells you how to adjust/change the various settings, but also explains the technical terminology in real English, so you know what those settings actually do when activated.
And if all that weren't enough, I scouted around a bit and bought the silver version (DV-610AV-S)of this unit for $30.00 less than the black one! (look for the one that ships for free with Amazon.com) Other than the color of the case, it is identical to the black one. I know, I looked them both up on Pioneer's web site and compared them point by point.
I do love the region-free feature too. But for me, this is more ho-hum, since I already owned one - a far inferior quality Philips one.
About the only thing I can think of to improve the user-friendliness of this product would be to have an alphabetized index in the manual. But, since it's only a 61 page manual, it's not such a big issue overall.
Another suggestion I would have would be to allow to record audio from DVDs also. So often, the audio track on a DVD sounds so much better than the soundtrack that is published on CD (i.e.: Brassed Off, Eyes Wide Shut), although I recognize there may be some copyright issues with that concept.
For the record: I am getting a second unit for my upstairs TV. Have I mentioned that I love it...? This is a really great product!!!
P.S.: Adding this comment on Jan. 17, 2010: I see the price difference between the black and the silver model is now up to $90.00!!! The silver one is the very same model, folks, but $ 90.00 cheaper!!! I am still just as enthused about this player as I was when I first reviewed it. I now own 2 units. Superb product!!!
text_fidelity_b: PIONEER DV-610V-K MULTI REGION 1080p UPCONVERTING DVD PLAYER

Technics Premium in- Ear Monitors IEM, High-Fidelity Wired in-Ear Earbuds Earphones with Innovative 10mm Driver for Ultra-Low Distortion - EAH-TZ700, Black/Gold I work in live AV production, and usually keep a pair of Sony over-the-ear headphones in my gear bag for monitoring sound on location. Quality of the sound is important for concert and other live music gigs. But those big Sonys take up a lot of space, so I've been considering a good set of IEMs for a while now. In the past I haven't had good results from anything that wasn't a large over-the-ear set, and I have small ears that reject a lot of ear-bud style devices so I was excited to get a chance to try these out.

Ok, to be fair, I don't have any other IEMs to compare this to, but I'm BLOWN AWAY at how incredible they sound at such a miniscule size. I put on the smallest tips for my ears and they actually stay in relatively well, and create the passive noise cancellation I was expecting but without being uncomfortable to wear for an extended period of time. But the range of sound reproduced was something I have only experienced in larger studio headphones!
A perk of IEMs versus larger headphones on jobs like mine are that I can pull out one so I can hear the sound around me while monitoring with my other ear (great if working with an audio engineer who needs to communicate with me on the job), and it comes with a pretty nifty case to wrap it up and slide into my bag. The case makes it bigger than it needs to be, but honestly this is so much less space than my old headphones took up, and keeps the cord from getting tangled. I love it!
For personal use, they sound great even on consumer equipment, but they really shine on devices that can drive the additional range such as my old LG V20 with it's Quad DAC built in (one of the reasons I keep that old device around!).
The price tag is a little steep for me personally, but my Sony headphones retail somewhere around this (I had bought them used), and I KNOW there are pricier options out there, so it seems to fit right into the audiophile equipment range.
text_fidelity_b: Technics Premium in- Ear Monitors IEM, High-Fidelity Wired in-Ear Earbuds Earphones with Innovative 10mm Driver for Ultra-Low Distortion - EAH-TZ700, Black/Gold

Mount-It! Single Monitor Arm Mount | Desk Stand | Heavy Duty Full Motion Height Adjustable | Fits 19 21 24 27 29 30 in VESA 75 100 Compatible Computer Screen | C-Clamp Base | Holds up to 33 Lbs I purchased this specifically to mount a [[ASIN:B00RPJOQQ8 ViewSonic VA2465smh 24-Inch SuperClear MVA LED Monitor]]. It definitely holds the monitor - steady - in any position within this mount's range. Note that my monitor weighs in around 9.5 pounds, so factor that into your own needs.

Assembly is a snap. It comes with everything you need to mount the VESA adapter to your monitor, including washers and spacers. I had anticipated having to purchase bolts to fit, but that turned out to be unnecessary.

One of the things I love is the VESA bracket has slots that fit into horizontal posts. Those support the full weight of the monitor while you are installing the two adjustment bolts. In other words, assembling, mounting and adjusting this can be done by one person. My mount shipped with thumb style bolts and optional, heavier ones that you can use with the included hex wrench. Since my monitor was so light to begin with I used the thumb bolts, which hold the viewing angle in the narrow range of movement the VESA mount allows. Had my monitor been heavier I would have probably used the hex bolts, which are a lot beefier.

Bottom line: read some of the other reviews that discuss challenges that this mount has for heavier and larger monitors. However, if you have a 24" that is in the 10-12 pound range (or less) this is all the mount that you need. It's built like a tank, is a breeze to assemble, and holds lighter monitors absolutely rock steady.
text_fidelity_b: Mount-It! Single Monitor Arm Mount | Desk Stand | Heavy Duty Full Motion Height Adjustable | Fits 19 21 24 27 29 30 in VESA 75 100 Compatible Computer Screen | C-Clamp Base | Holds up to 33 Lbs

I'll be using this lens and the D5600 as a portrait backup for my Pentax K-1-II and the AF-D* 50mm f/1.4 AW lens. At the price of this Nikon "nifty fifty" it's a great investment.

UPDATE 12/05/22:
I had my music playing on ALL Echoes, including the ECHO SHOW 10, in a loop play, when everything stopped in mid-song, to show the Jeopardy ad!!!! Seriously?! Damn Echo Show 10 and 8, are going back while the returns are available. With my refunds, I'm buying the new larger Google Nest with NO ADS. Furious!!! text_fidelity_a:
B-Land 10" Ring Light with Tripod Stand & 3 Phone Holders & Flexible Clip Microphone Holder for Multicam Live Stream, LED YouTube Lighting Kit Photo Light for Videos & Photography I am best described as a skilled amateur when it comes to photography and I am always looking for ways to get better and to build my knowledge and ability. I am not a professional by any means, but I know a lot more than the average selfie-taker. I have wanted a ring light for a little while and I was delighted to have the chance to get to use this one. It does work, in the right circumstances, but it is definitely aimed at the base consumer market and is priced accordingly.

Thought it can be used as part of a professional set-up, it is designed and marketed as a consumer-grade unit. There are a number of obvious design decisions that make this more than just a little apparent. The tripod is good, but the mounts are designed for smartphones and will not work for DSLR cameras, mirrorless cameras or video cameras. That’s ok, as it is clearly marketed that way. The unit uses a USB power source which is an important point – the light itself isn’t especially bright like one that uses a normal AC power source. To be effective, the light needs to be fairly close to the subject. If a dim directional light is needed, a regular desk lamp is more than adequate in most cases. The upshot is that using USB power makes it much more portable for travel (more on that in a moment).

The remote allows for making a few adjustments to the light itself. There are three color modes and ten brightness modes, all of which can be (rather, must be) set through the remote. The adjustments are sufficient for this grade of light, though I would have found more colors and a more smooth graduation in brightness to be more useful. That’s more of a nitpick than a criticism considering the price point.

Build-wise, this unit is acceptable. It should hold up well enough in the studio or home office. What is lacking is a carry case to protect it when travelling. Considering the target audience (social media producers), this is an oversight that I think is important. To transport this light, it should be well secured and the only recourse as sold is to put it back in the original box, and that’s just unwieldy. Plan accordingly if you choose to transport this light.

This is an adequate unit for its target audience but will leave the aspiring professional underwhelmed. If you are looking for something that will work sufficiently for making posts to social media this is a reasonable unit; if you need a serious ring light for photography, consider other options. The main problem with this light is the fact that it is designed for portability but comes with no carrying case; keep this in mind.
text_fidelity_b: B-Land 10" Ring Light with Tripod Stand & 3 Phone Holders & Flexible Clip Microphone Holder for Multicam Live Stream, LED YouTube Lighting Kit Photo Light for Videos & Photography

Yankok [The Ultimate Pass Through Crimper] for CAT5/5e CAT6 Network Connectors CAT6a CAT7 Shielded Modular Plugs RJ45 RJ12 RJ11 Pass Through Crimp Tool (Strip Cut and Crimp All-in-One. Red Handle) While I was a bit intimidated at the idea of making my own Ethernet cables, once I got this set and did a bit of research I found it really isn’t near as difficult as I thought it may be.

If this is your first time doing this here is the cable I recommend: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B01JAVMVQ0/ref=cm_sw_em_r_mt_dp_ADqVFbYVVKVD6
It is important to look for “SOLID BARE COPPER CONDUCTORS” as this will make an enormous difference in the performance of your cable. The above cable listed works incredibly well and will not let you down.

I chose to create my own Ethernet cables as I was running cables to PoE security cameras and I wanted them the exact length so I could run them as far as I needed and not have excess that caused transmission delays.

Adding the pass through connectors and crimping them is quite easy once you get the hang of it. Watch a video and take your time as you begin. This tool is well made and will hold up to years of use.

Unlike the majority of crimping tools this one will allow you to crimp and create RJ45 Cat 3/4/5/5e/6 (8x8) (8P8C), RJ12 6-position (6x6) (6P6C), RJ11 4-position (6x4) (6P4C) and RJ11 2-position (6x2) (6P2C). This is definitely one of the most versatile crimping tools I have seen.

While I was using it I had a bit of issue when stripping the wires as it can be a bit tricky to get a clean strip. After creating several wires I found I got better at this and was able to strip more efficiently.

I have been very pleased with this set and would recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Yankok [The Ultimate Pass Through Crimper] for CAT5/5e CAT6 Network Connectors CAT6a CAT7 Shielded Modular Plugs RJ45 RJ12 RJ11 Pass Through Crimp Tool (Strip Cut and Crimp All-in-One. Red Handle)
