Philips - Hue Play Starter Kit - Black First effort at setup was very frustrating, so I waited a day and started over.

The lights are powerful and intelligently designed. I did not buy them for the tv reason other people do. I just wanted a colorful backdrop for my FaceTime calls. In setting these up, I ended up crippling a few of my lights in a way that they now only offer about 9 colors, which is a problem I'll have to fix.

I agree with others, the cords to these a). shouldn't be proprietary, and b) shouldn't be black. They should be white to blend in with a wall. So I'll be buying a skinny extension cord to make up for that. Maybe they can change that for future customers.

The fact that the lights must both be plugged in to the same source is a definite buzzkill. And like everyone else who loves Hue, I have about 20 lights in my small place.

Once set up, I liked them a lot. They do all the colors and are fairly flexible with Alexa on the dimming, even more so on the app. But I don't recommend putting the app on the same network as your computer, these lights are VERY easy to hack, and if they do get hacked, they can get into your computer. The FBI warned against all iot (internet of things) devices like this.
text_fidelity_b: Philips - Hue Play Starter Kit - Black

text_fidelity_a:
G-TiDE Kids Tablet, 10.1 inch Android 11 Tablet for Kids, 32GB ROM, Quad-Core, HD Dual Camera, WiFi Bluetooth, Parental Control, Kids App Klap with Kid-Proof Case and Screen Protector, Blue I actually just had an opportunity to try the pink version of this tablet, which you can find under a different listing here. It's an identical tablet from the same brand with a different colored case outside. Which is a GOOD thing, because I actually really like the tablet underneath, and the case it comes in!
It's not cutting edge hardware, but its fast enough to do anything kid related easily. The cameras aren't great, but again- at this price you shouldn't expect them to be Galaxy S or iPad camera. But the actual user experience is pretty good despite the cheap price tag.
For starters you get Android 11 out of the box, which is pretty incredible to find on an inexpensive device. It also comes with some pretty excellent kid software that parents can use to control and offer fun, entertaining and educational games and apps.
The case is the best part, however, as it is thick and "kid proof", as they say on the box. There's a stand that be adjusted or used as a handle, and overall gives you something substantial to hold onto. The only thing I'm not crazy about is that the case makes the holes and buttons a little bit difficult to reach/line up. The case is very thick, as we already said, so sometimes plugging in, say, a USB OTG plug with a keyboard is a little difficult to line up in the hole. And the power button isn't in a great place for little fingers to find quickly. But these are minor details, it is still a pretty great tablet that will work well for kids.
text_fidelity_b: G-TiDE Kids Tablet, 10.1 inch Android 11 Tablet for Kids, 32GB ROM, Quad-Core, HD Dual Camera, WiFi Bluetooth, Parental Control, Kids App Klap with Kid-Proof Case and Screen Protector, Blue

Sangean WR-2 AM / FM-RBDS Wooden Cabinet Digital Tuning Radio (Black) First of all, my first order arrived with a small crack in the wooden cabinet and it would not turn on. I am going to give Sangean the benefit of the doubt and assume that it was shipping damage even though the box from the outside did not look like it was damaged, so I won't let this affect my rating.

But this did give me a chance to test Amazon's return policy, and I must say it was great. When I realized that I had to return the radio, I went to Amazon's website and clicked on the radio and selected "return." Then I was prompted to print a return shipping label to attach to the box when I sent it back. By the time I did that, there was an email in my in box from Amazon telling me that they were shipping a replacement to me via UPS Air. So I packed up the unit in it's original box, attached the label I had printed, and then the next day when the replacement arrived I gave the box to the UPS driver. Of course, all of this was at no additional cost to me. I was quite impressed with the whole process.

Now to the radio itself. Overall I am quite impressed with it and I am giving it four stars. For a radio of it's size, it sounds great. I have never heard a radio that small with the tight bass response that this one has. And AM radio sounds better than than it does even on my Onkyo receiver that I have in my family room.

The radio with it's wooden cabinet looks great on my nightstand and you can just tell by looking at it that it is a quality product.

The tuner's sensitivity on the FM band is good with the external wire antenna that is supplied with it. Selectivity between adjacent stations is also good. And I am getting good stereo separation when I listen with headphones. I do have one small quibble however. There is a button to switch any FM station to mono, but you have to do this individually for each station. It would have been better if you could toggle between stereo and mono for all the stations at once rather than having to do it individually for each one.

AM sensitivity is pretty good using the built in antenna. Weak stations in my area come in better than they did with my old clock radio, but I still do have some problems with the very weak stations. I could probably improve this if I bought a good external AM antenna, but I don't think I will bother to do that since I don't really listen to any of the weak stations anyway.

One reason why I got this radio was because it has a line in jack. I have connected my Directv box to it so that I can listen to the Directv music channels through the radio without having my TV set on. All I had to do was to go to Radio Shack and buy a Y adapter with two RCA plugs on one end and a 1/8" plug on the other. It works like a charm.

I also like that the display has large enough numerals that I can read it without my glasses on. However, as others have mentioned, the display defaults to the radio station frequency or the RDS display rather than to the time. To get the time display back I have to tap the display button, and it's hard to do at night in a dark room. I think it would have been better if it defaulted to the time in the first place.

Another quibble that I have is that the power button uses a bright blue light which is distracting in a dark room. They shouldn't have made it so bright. That will take some getting used to.

Also, as others have mentioned, setting the alarm is needlessly complicated as is turning it off. You need to hit three different buttons to do it. I am starting to get the hang of it, but I wish they would have just included a button which toggles the alarm on and off.

But overall I am rating this as a good four star product that could use some minor improvements. The most important thing to me is the sound quality, and that is unmatched for a radio of this size.
text_fidelity_b: Sangean WR-2 AM / FM-RBDS Wooden Cabinet Digital Tuning Radio (Black)

Munitio SV Mobile Performance Earphones with 3 Button Mic Control, Bronze Lower and mid end earphones have generally been lacking in both quality and performance. Given my propensity to misplace them, I have been reluctant to invest in more expensive versions. But with increased reliance on mobile devices, it was most definitely time to upgrade.

My familiarity with Munitio was more from their urban chic style complete with bullet motif, Kevlar coated cord, "tactical" carrying case and "hollow point" ear cups. At the risk of looking more Duck dynasty than cool, I was eager to try them.

Designed for use with Apple devices, the phones come securely packaged in a black carrying case. The look is sleek and modern and the bronze color is appealing. These are also available in black and gray. There are three sets of ear cups in different sizes. They were comfortable and shut out outside noise. The cord is flat and tangle free with a heft that promises durability. The 3 button mic control is located on the upper left hand side of the earphone cable. I really couldn't see the buttons but quickly mastered them by touch. They provide full functionality for calls and music on iPods, iPods and iPhones and just music for other mp3 players and Android devices.

I encountered no difficulties in making or taking calls. I could hear the other party and they could hear me without difficulty. The mic is positioned close enough to the mouth and is sufficiently sensitive that I didn't have to scream or repeat things. I made calls from a fairly busy coffee shop and a mall and ambient noise did not impair the call quality.

I tried these earphones with my IPod and a cheap mp3 player of dubious lineage. The sound was clear, strong and enjoyable. I did not find the bass overwhelming and was generally pleased with the performance.

Bottom line, I liked these earphones. The case and the trio of ear cups are thoughtful touches. Although light, there is a sense of substance and quality. The controls are intuitive and easy to use. There is a two year limited warranty. Serving up generous doses of comfort, convenience and performance, these ear phones are right on target.
text_fidelity_b: Munitio SV Mobile Performance Earphones with 3 Button Mic Control, Bronze

Certified Refurbished Kindle Paperwhite E-reader - White, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers (Previous Generation - 7th) I stopped reading as much when my eyes got old and tired. I finally broke down and bought a Kindle, and it's been a game-changer. I'm blowing through books again! Overall, it's been very helpful.

Pros and cons are:

Pros:
- can enlarge fonts as needed so it's easier on my eyes
- Paperwhite backlighting is also really easy on the eyes; I don't get fatigued and can read anywhere, night or day
- can download a crap ton of books and only carry the one small device
- great battery life

Cons:
- miss the tactile aspect of turning pages, skipping back and forth, feeling in your hands how much book you have left
- can't remember as well where a passage is in the book because I don't have mental image of where it was on the page, and about how many pages in it was
- touchscreen is kind of spazzy and sometimes will change font size on me or if I accidentally brush against the screen while reading -- this has been the most annoying bit
- touchscreen is also kind of slow: I touch something, it takes a moment to react; by this time I think it hasn't registered so I touch it again, only to have it do something twice and take me somewhere else, and I end up lost

Generally speaking though, the pros outweigh the cons, so I will keep loading books on this little guy!

text_fidelity_a: SkipDr DVD and CD Manual Disc Repair System, Single I was a little nervous about this product given the mixed reviews. It comes with the machine, a solution, and a rubbing cloth.  My daughters favorite Disney movie was scratched and skipping a lot so I wanted to fix it.  I wet the cd with the solution and placed it in the machine.  The machine has to be set on a hard flat service. I tried to just hold it in the air and it would not work. I made one round and then reapplied the solution, then cranked the machine around again.  (It goes slowly). I buffed the DVD with the cloth as directed and played the DVD. It skipped less than before, but was still skipping.  I repeated the entire process again, and now the DVD works perfectly!.  I want to try this on some very scratched  DVDs and see how far I can push it. I would recommend this for mild to moderately scratched DVDs/ CDs at this point.  Remember it says it is very important to keep the disc wet with the solution the entire time and rub it throughly with the cloth or it will not work, so do not skip those steps.

Avantree DG40SA Dedicated Windows 10 Bluetooth USB Adapter, Wireless Dongle for PC Bought with Win 10, Plug & Play, Support Headpones, PS4 Gaming Controllers, Mouse, Keyboard, Printers etc. I purchased a Lenovo Ideacentre AIO Y910 in December 2017 and it had a beautiful built-in Qualcomm bluetooth function. It worked great. I had my desktop paired with my Echo Dots and with Alexa could continue listening to movies/music/podcasts/youtube anywhere in my house away from the computer. Along came a Windows 10 update in March 2018 that disabled/removed the bluetooth function/drivers ENTIRELY. No roll backs/restores, or reinstallations brought it back. The internal bluetooth function was completely ruined and prevented from running. I was furious and microsoft support was zero help. I finally begrudgingly purchased this to do the same function. I'm angry I had to pay for something I already paid for my computer to have, and that I have to waste a USB spot for it, but it works, was truly plug and play, though the connecting of all my speakers/Echo Dots is more complicated that previously. For example, with the original bluetooth capabilities, I could chose to have one or both of the Dots automatically connect when bluetooth was enabled. I could have them play together or verbally tell Alexa to connect/disconnect. Now for some reason with this bluetooth, voice control doesn't work, Alexa can't disconnect (she will do it but then it automatically reconnects) and if one Dot is connected the other won't. I have to run back to my computer's bluetooth settings and pair/unpair and connect/disconnect each time I want to make a change. This is frustrating. If anyone knows of anyway to circumvent this or the original bluetooth death please let me know, I'd be forever grateful.

The range for the device is fine, I live in a 1200 sq ft two story townhome and there was no issue with my computer seeing the Dot in the bedroom or the Dot downstairs. Connections are strong.

text_fidelity_a:
Tribit Bluetooth Speaker, XSound Go Speaker with 16W Loud Sound & Deeper Bass, 24H Playtime, IPX7 Waterproof, Bluetooth 5.0 TWS Pairing Portable Wireless Speaker for Home, Outdoor (Upgraded) In full disclosure, I must admit that I miss my Bose Bluetooth speaker. Their acoustics are impeccable. The "Tribit XSound Go Bluetooth Speakers" only cost a fraction of my Bose speaker. I first purchased the "DOSS Touch Wireless Bluetooth" which is in the same price range; I returned that product because it lacked bass and was unimpressive overall. The Tribit, however, has plenty of bass for such a small speaker. Ironically, the problem that I have is the treble! I think it is an inherent problem with smaller speakers and not this particular device. I have installed an equalizer on my computer which mitigates some of the problems and makes the speaker sound very acceptable.

The pros:
• The speaker is loud! It is perfect for a jam session in your bedroom. I'm not sure it is suitable for large or multi rooms.
• The quality is good, and the speaker looks like a million bucks.
• It has an excellent microphone that works well with phone calls and even to interact with Siri or Cortana.
• The Play button allows one to answer, reject or end a call. It also can play or pause a song. Finally, it allows you to skip a music track forward or backward.

The cons:
• While the bass is fairly impressive, the treble is slightly overriding.
• The battery does not nearly last for 24 hours if you like to blast music as I do
• The speaker can only be paired to one device at a time. If you are listening to music on the computer and the phone tries to connect, the speaker will sometimes disconnect from all devices. The speaker does have an av input one could connect to the computer but obviously, the speaker would no longer be completely portable. This could be a deal breaker for many.

After comparing this speaker with others in its price range, I realize that this speaker has such poor sound quality that I could never recommend it to anyone.
text_fidelity_b: Tribit Bluetooth Speaker, XSound Go Speaker with 16W Loud Sound & Deeper Bass, 24H Playtime, IPX7 Waterproof, Bluetooth 5.0 TWS Pairing Portable Wireless Speaker for Home, Outdoor (Upgraded)

text_fidelity_a:
Blink Indoor Home Security Camera System with Motion Detection, HD Video, 2-Year Battery Life and Cloud Storage Included - 3 Camera Kit In terms of installation, it really doesn't get any easier: basically just plug in the control module and tap a couple buttons to register each camera and you're in business. Took me all of 5 minutes.

The cameras themselves aren't feature rich - you're not going to find tilt/swivel/zoom or even night vision. But you can't expect it from cameras that operate in 2 AA for up to 2 years! They do what they're designed to do: basic monitoring with motion detection in a completely wireless setup (you can literally place the cameras anywhere!). An LED light can illuminate any recording in darkness.

There's no monthly service fee either - but the recordings you can take are only up to a minute long and there's a limit on how many.

I love these cameras for their ease of setup and complete mobility. The only reason I'm not giving them 5 stars is the lack of an outdoor camera option and a little bit buggy iOS app.

Update (11/27/2017): a couple negatives to the cameras:
(1) while each camera comes with a wall mount, orienting it just right (in my case on a front porch so I could see who's at the door) isn't all that easy (just because the camera doesn't have an area in its view doesn't mean it won't detect motion slightly outside it!)
(2) the cameras have no speakers. I knew this when buying, of course, but competing cameras in same price range do.
(3) I just asked Blink whether there are any plans for Apple HomeKIt support - and there aren't :-( This is a big negative for me because I'm starting to do some home automation and since we're an Apple household, I want HomeKit. So I'm going to be looking for another set of cameras instead of expanding my Blink set :-(
text_fidelity_b: Blink Indoor Home Security Camera System with Motion Detection, HD Video, 2-Year Battery Life and Cloud Storage Included - 3 Camera Kit

text_fidelity_a:
RCA RD1006 Discwasher D4+ Vinyl Record Care System This is the best record cleaning I tried so far. I is very effective in removing dust (and associated static noise) from records that are in reasonably good shape. Of course, it cannot repair records which have been damaged due to being played while dirty. If you acquire a used record in dirty condition, it is probably a good idea to wash it with distilled water first before using the discwasher on it.

I noticed that there are several one-star reviews complaining about the direction of fibers on the cleaning pad that comes with this system. Yes, the cords of the corduroy-like microfiber material does run along the edge of the brush, but this is actually how it should be to provide even coverage across all the grooves. The cords of any fabric is much too thick to fit into the actual grooves on the record. If the cords were to run along the direction of the the grooves, some grooves would be cleaned and some wouldn't. Having the cords being perpendicular to the grooves on the record ensures that all grooves get cleaned evenly. After all, it is the microfibers, not the cords of the fabric, doing the cleaning.

Another advantage of cords running perpendicular to the grooves of the record is that, as you slowly rotate the brush on its axis (as shown in the provided directions), dust that has been collected gets trapped between the cords that are being lifted off the record as the next (clean) cord of the fabric starts making contact with the record surface.
text_fidelity_b: RCA RD1006 Discwasher D4+ Vinyl Record Care System

Belkin VideoLink 3 Powerline Internet Adapter We tried this internet adapter in quite a few ways in our home and came to the conclusion that it is a great lower cost alternative for large homes that want to have internet around but don't have the ability to have it around the house available for whatever reason.

This works well most of the time- performance is like that of our hardline and wi-fi connections. Download and upload times were the same and smoothness of operation was also good. The only problem we had was occasionally it would cease working for a minute.

It is hard to tell why this happened- it was erratic and not predictable. Heavy machinery in the house did not seem to affect it, nor did other fluctuations of power usage. However, that workability of the internet did get affected on a few occasions, but I am not sure why. It could have been our internet or it could have been the adapter.

All in all, it is a good less expensive alternative to running expensive wire around a large home to give access to the internet. It does take up an electrical outlet for each unit, however, which could be frustrating in some situations.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin VideoLink 3 Powerline Internet Adapter

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin Portable Friction Mount - Frustration Free Packaging I have a Nuvi 360. It came with a suction cup windshield mount. It also came with a steel disk with double sticky adhesive on the back. I was supposed to mount this disk somewhere on my dashboard, then use the suction cup to attach the mount. I didn't want to use the suction mount directly onto the windshield because 1) it telegraphs the presence of an expensive GPS unit, 2) it's illegal in California to attach anything to the windshield and 3) I don't think the suction cup would last very long.

Then there's the disk with the very permanent double sticky tape. The problem with almost all cars these days is there really isn't anywhere to attach the disk discreetly. Every square inch is taken with existing stuff. And who wants an ugly disk glued to the dash anyway? And what if I want to use the GPS in other vehicles? More disks?

So I settled on this "beanbag" mount with the ball mount arm.

Unfortunately, before the beanbag friction mount arrived, I was flexing the arm in the suction cup mount and noticed the suction cup's mounting bracket had already broken. I had never even attached it to anything! The mount is beautifully engineered and built...except for one area where the arm's hinge pin attaches to the suction cup's plastic hinge loops. The loops are too thin and fragile. The loops cracked and broke with hardly any hinging at all.

So now I have a quite useless suction mount but a very functional ball arm. What to do?

I drove the hinge pin out of the ball arm. Then I took two small 1" x 1" steel angle brackets and attached them to the ball arm with a 2" long, 8-32 threaded machine screw and an 8-32 wingnut. This created two "feet" for the ball arm. Then I epoxied the two bracket "feet" to the fabric (upper) side of an old 1/4" thick mousepad. Ta da. A friction pad for pennies with a ball arm attached.

Works great. Cost was virtually nothing. Doesn't slide on either of the two dashboards I've tried it on. The mousepad is flexible and conforms easily to the curving shape of the various dashboards. It doesn't weigh much but the thick mousepad has enough heft to plant the getup nicely. The grippy rubber side of the mousepad adheres nicely to the dash. Yet I can pull it down to the floor quickly and reposition it easily.

I wish I'd thought of this BEFORE I ordered this "official" friction mount to the tune of a couple of twenties.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin Portable Friction Mount - Frustration Free Packaging

text_fidelity_a:
Jabra Evolve 40 MS Professional Wired Headset, Mono – Telephone Headset for Greater Productivity, Superior Sound for Calls and Music, 3.5mm Jack/USB Connection, All-Day Comfort Design, MS Optimized These headphones are the most comfortable I have ever owned. The ear cups sit flat against the ear, which feels more natural than the usual headphone with ear cups that surround your ear with a hot and sweaty dome. I could only handle that style for a while and then my ears needed a cool off to dry out. If you are using these headphones somewhere loud, like a train stop, the environment noises will interfere a bit, same if you turn the volume up bystanders will hear it. But the lack of hot and sweaty ears is such a bonus so these other problems are easily avoided.

The headphones are instantly compatible with all smartphones with a headphone jack. I used it on a Google Pixel and on iPhone 5's the sound quality was crystal clear, much better than any bluetooth headset I've ever had, and I've had plenty.

The USB adapter with the call controls worked great for my business calls GoToMeeting, Skype for Business and Google Voice.

The cord is three feet long, perfect for me since I get tired of getting the cord tangled as I pace around during calls, but it might be a bit on the short side for some. For use with the computer the USB adds two feet between the USB port and the controlling buttons. The cord is round, and so far, has been resistant to kinks.

The volume and mute buttons are on the cord instead of the headset, I like this because I don't have to memorize the placement during a call and the indicator light for mute keeps me from forgetting that I have muted a call and no one can hear me because I muted to sneeze, cough or shush my cat.

The only drawback is that unlike with a bluetooth headset there are no volume or mute controls as part of the headset or cord when it is plugged into a smart phone.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra Evolve 40 MS Professional Wired Headset, Mono – Telephone Headset for Greater Productivity, Superior Sound for Calls and Music, 3.5mm Jack/USB Connection, All-Day Comfort Design, MS Optimized

text_fidelity_a:
Denon DHT-T110 TV Speaker Base with Bluetooth aptX Streaming and Dolby Digital Decoding I'm having a serious problem with the Denon DHT-T110 TV Speaker Base that apparently the other reviewers are not having. I called Denon Technical Support and after spending a lot of time behind the TV set making sure all the wires were hooked up correctly and then pressing different buttons on the Denon Speaker base, they can't figure out what is causing this problem. And the problem is this: No sound signal is going to the Denon speaker base through the TV from the Roku player. The Roku works just fine through the regular TV speakers and is connected directly to the TV via HDMI. When the input on the TV is set to stream via the Roku no sound comes through the Denon and it turns off. If I increase the volume on the TV speakers you hear sound. If the input is changed to TV with the TV sound off, sound will come through the Denon. Also, if a DVD is played on the DVD player which is connected to the TV, the sound comes through the Denon. It just won't put out sound when the Roku input is being used. And that's a real bummer for me because we watch a lot of Netflix and Amazon streaming through our Roku. I am using the digital optical cord included with the Denon Speaker Base. I have it connected to the Digital Optical "Out" on the back of my Sharp 37" flat screen TV to the digital optical "In" on the back of the Denon Speaker Base.

I will keep working on this problem, and if anyone reading this has any idea that might fix it please say so in the comments section. I would love very much to have it work and to raise the star level to 5. When sound does come through the Denon it's great! Loud, clear and no buzzes or rattles whatsoever like when the volume is turned all the way up when using the TV speakers. I love that it can get loud and there's no rattles or weird vibrations. and the night mode is very useful since the TV room is located underneath the main bedroom and my husband has to go to bed early since he has to go to work early. I like to stay up late and watch Netflix/Amazon or other streaming channels through the Roku (oops! That doesn't work through the Denon) and I keep the volume down lest it wake him up. I was really looking forward to using the Denon night sound function.

The Denon tech suggested hooking everything up to another TV to see if the problem is the Roku player or my TV. Unfortunately, I don't have another TV to test out the units to try and isolate the lack of sound from the Roku player to the Denon. I was really wanting to use this for night listening, but since I can't I will take the Denon to my mom's nursing home and hook it up to her small, flat-screen TV. Since she's half deaf, it might can help her hear the sound better. I will update this review afterwards.
text_fidelity_b: Denon DHT-T110 TV Speaker Base with Bluetooth aptX Streaming and Dolby Digital Decoding

text_fidelity_a:
ViewSonic VA2359-SMH 23 Inch IPS 1080p LED Monitor with HDMI and VGA Inputs What I like about this monitor:
1. Easy to set up - I used my previous monitor video cable and power cord and had it up and running in a few minutes.
2. Very clear resolution despite having an old video card.
3. It has an HDMI connection but I am using the regular VGA input and it still very clear.
4. A VGA and sound cord are included.
5. Very sleek, streamline black design which goes nicely with my other computer accessories.

What could be better:
1. The included instructions tell you nothing about how to make video and audio adjustments. I can't use a bright setting and it took a good while to figure out how to use the buttons underneath the screen. They are not intuitive at all.
2. Poor Audio - if you want good audio from this monitor that will not be possible. It is a thin monitor and the audio is very thin and tinny. I was hoping I could disconnect my external sound system to make more room on my desk but found out that I must keep it if I want to hear any decent sound from my computer.
3. While testing the volume on this monitor you must still figure out how to toggle using the various buttons underneath. There is no single volume button or toggle switch. And it will not get very loud.
4. If you don't bump the monitor or use the toggle switches the monitor stays fairly steady on it's stand. Otherwise it will rock and jiggle while using the buttons.
5. No HDMI cable is included.

The scant instructions did say to visit their website to download the latest drivers but as of yet this monitor is not listed in their driver drop down window. I don't think that matter much at this time as the monitor is very clear and sharp.
Overall: Good monitor for the price (as of this review it costs $138.24 Prime) which I feel is a fair price.
text_fidelity_b: ViewSonic VA2359-SMH 23 Inch IPS 1080p LED Monitor with HDMI and VGA Inputs
